# Contributing to agent-rules-kit

How to change the kit: where content goes, versioning, checks and evals. Sessions that work inside this repository read this file before a change; the always-on rules come from the installed `guardrails` plugin, so the root carries no `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` (KIT-042).

## Outside contributors

This section is for people outside the project; the rest of the file is the procedure the maintainer and agent sessions follow.

- One person maintains the kit for their own projects, so a change is weighed against the setups it already serves. Answers come as time allows.
- Start with an issue, using the [bug report](https://github.com/ChristianPrzybulinski/agent-rules-kit/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml) or the [rule or skill proposal](https://github.com/ChristianPrzybulinski/agent-rules-kit/issues/new?template=rule_or_skill_proposal.yml) form. A bug report names the kit `VERSION`, the agent with its version and the operating system.
- Open a pull request only after the maintainer agrees to the change in its issue; a pull request without one may be closed unreviewed. Link the issue, keep to one concern, add a line under `## [Unreleased]` in [`CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md), run `platforms/tools/check.sh` and fill in the PR checklist. The rest of this file says where each kind of content goes.
- A contribution is licensed under the repository's [MIT license](../LICENSE).
- Report a vulnerability privately, as [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) says, never in an issue or pull request.
- Everyone taking part follows the [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md), the Contributor Covenant 3.0.

## What goes where

| Content | Location |
|---|---|
| always-on global behavior | `plugins/guardrails/AGENTS.md` |
| hook guard, format/lint and the other hooks | `plugins/guardrails/hooks/hooks.json`; a hook too long for an inline command, the path-rule hook, is a script beside it (`path_rules.py`, KIT-081 stage 3) |
| path-triggered rule | `plugins/<plugin>/rules/<name>.md` in the owning plugin |
| coding standard | its always/never as a path rule, its procedure as a reference of the SDD step that applies it (`sdd-plan` or `sdd-implement`; a stack gets a `references/<stack>/` folder with a `README.md` index), never a skill nobody invokes (KIT-070) |
| procedure or reference | `plugins/<plugin>/skills/<name>/` |
| subagent profile | `plugins/<plugin>/agents/<name>.md` in the plugin whose skills consume it |
| artifact skeleton | `plugins/<plugin>/templates/<prefix>-<name>.md` |
| executable, schema or project kit | `platforms/` |
| design principles, consumer layout, KIT records | `docs/` |
| contributing guide, security policy, code of conduct | `.github/` (keeps the root to the README, license, changelog and version) |

## Invariants

`platforms/ci/validations/check_kit.py` enforces these:

- The repository root holds no agent-facing content. A root `AGENTS.md` is refused: the root is the Devin meta-plugin, so it would load in every Devin session on top of `plugins/guardrails/AGENTS.md`.
- `.devin-plugin/plugin.json` requires every plugin and lists none as optional.
- Every directory under `plugins/` is a plugin with `.devin-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `plugin.json` and a generated `INDEX.md`; no other `INDEX.md` exists in this repository. The rule is the kit repository's own: a consumer project that enables `check_docs_structure.py` keeps an `INDEX.md` in each `done/` folder (KIT-074).
- `plugins/guardrails/` is the only plugin with `AGENTS.md` or `hooks/`.
- Plugin names are unique, and every referenced skill or agent is reachable through the dependency graph.
- `VERSION`, the meta-plugin manifest and every Devin, Codex and Claude manifest agree.
- Codex and Claude marketplace source paths are `./plugins/<name>`; plugin content has no managed duplicate.
- The Claude marketplace `renames` map sends each retired plugin name to its successor (or `null`), so an installed old name migrates on the next session (KIT-038).

## Versioning

A release sets one version in [`VERSION`](../VERSION), in every manifest `"version"` field and in a [`CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md) heading, then tags `vX.Y.Z`. The steps, in order:

1. Bump, on a branch from current `main` with a clean tree: `python3 platforms/tools/bump_version.py X.Y.Z` (KIT-019). It refuses a version that is not SemVer or not above `VERSION`, a dirty tree and an empty `## [Unreleased]`. It writes `VERSION`, replaces `"version": "<current>"` in every tracked `*plugin.json` and `*marketplace.json` (printing the count) and inserts `## [X.Y.Z] - <today>` under `## [Unreleased]` (`--date YYYY-MM-DD` overrides the date). Then run `check.sh`.
2. Open the release PR `chore(release): publish X.Y.Z`. Its body's `## Red` opens with `Exception: manual: a version bump only; no executable behavior changes.`: the PR changes no test file, so the `red` job fails a NONE without that line (#294).
3. After the merge, confirm that `ci-full.yml` is green on the merge commit (`gh run list --workflow ci-full.yml --commit <sha>`), then tag it on `main` with an annotated tag: `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m vX.Y.Z <commit>`, then `git push origin vX.Y.Z`. `release.yml` publishes no release from a commit without a green `ci-full` run, and the ruleset `protect-release-tags` keeps the tag, so a tag pushed too early waits for a re-run of `release.yml` (KIT-077).
4. Pushing the tag runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which validates tag == `VERSION`, creates the release from the CHANGELOG section and, last, moves the `stable` branch to the released commit, fast-forward only (KIT-081): every install follows `stable` (the Claude Code and Codex marketplaces, Devin's team plugin, a project's `extraKnownMarketplaces`), so that move is what delivers the release. Never create the release by hand while that run is going: one of the two creates then fails. Only when the run has ended (`gh run list --workflow release.yml --limit 1`) and `gh release view vX.Y.Z` finds no release, publish it by hand with the same notes and the workflow's title format: `python3 platforms/tools/bump_version.py --notes X.Y.Z > /tmp/kit-notes.md`, then `gh release create vX.Y.Z --verify-tag --title vX.Y.Z --notes-file /tmp/kit-notes.md`, then move `stable` the way the workflow does: `gh api -X PATCH repos/ChristianPrzybulinski/agent-rules-kit/git/refs/heads/stable -f sha="$(git rev-parse 'vX.Y.Z^{commit}')" -F force=false`. A refused move (not a fast-forward) means `stable` holds a commit the release does not contain; find out why before moving it.

The layout of 10.x, kept unchanged by 11.0.0, is frozen until at least 2027-01-01 (principle "Layout stability" in [docs/design.md](../docs/design.md)). A layout or installation-destination change is a SemVer MAJOR change and ships with a deprecation note in the release notes plus a migration in `bootstrap.sh` and `doctor.sh`. A content change is MINOR when it adds a rule, skill, reference, template, validator gate or document, and PATCH when it corrects one without changing routing. There is no separate layout version.

## Adding content

| Type | Steps |
|---|---|
| kit feature | only for a hook, `plugins/guardrails/AGENTS.md`, plugin structure or manifests, a check, gate or script behavior change, or a new or removed skill: after the owner confirms it, skill `sdd-plan` writes the FEAT `docs/spec/features/KIT-NNN.md` from template `spec-feature-lite.md` (the kit runs the FEAT-only flow, `project.kind: tooling`, KIT-101; the process: [`docs/features/README.md`](../docs/features/README.md)), with issue `[KIT-NNN] <title>` and label `kit-feature`; the implementing PR closes the issue, `spec_trace.py sync-status` derives the FEAT status from that PR and its CHANGELOG line cites `KIT-NNN`. A follow-up that corrects the behaviour a delivered FEAT shipped amends that FEAT's record (Scope, CA, Decisions, History) instead of opening a new FEAT (precedent: #406, #416, #417). Any other change (a skill, rule, reference, template or doc text edit) needs only a CHANGELOG line, and the PR body carries the why |
| rule | create `plugins/<plugin>/rules/<name>.md` in the owning plugin with `description`, `trigger: glob|model_decision|manual`, and `globs` for a glob rule (with `paths` equal to them, which the path-rule hook matches with `**/`, `**`, `*` and `?`); body = one pointer line to the skill or step reference that holds the procedure, then always/never bullets, at most 40 lines (the same body goes into the generated folder `AGENTS.md` block for Codex, KIT-067, and into the path-rule hook's context for Claude Code, KIT-081 stage 3); give it a line in `plugins/guardrails/hooks/sync-profiles.txt` naming the profiles that receive it; run `python3 platforms/tools/gen_index.py` to list it in the plugin's `INDEX.md` (never add non-rule files to `rules/` — Devin loads every `.md` there as a rule) |
| skill | search `plugins/guardrails/INDEX.md` first and extend the skill that owns the topic; a new skill is only for a topic no skill owns (KIT-039) that someone calls on its own; a standard is a rule plus a step reference (KIT-070). Copy [`docs/templates/kit-skill.md`](../docs/templates/kit-skill.md) to `plugins/<plugin>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; user-only means exactly `triggers: [user]`, Codex `agents/openai.yaml` with implicit invocation disabled, and Claude `disable-model-invocation: true`; run `python3 platforms/tools/gen_index.py` (it copies the description into the plugin's `INDEX.md`) |
| reference | copy [`docs/templates/kit-reference.md`](../docs/templates/kit-reference.md) to `plugins/<plugin>/skills/<owner>/references/<topic>.md`; set `kind: fact` with date/sources or `kind: detail`; keep ≤60 lines and link it from `SKILL.md`; a `references/<folder>/` holds references of one stack plus a `README.md` index that `SKILL.md` names as `<folder>/README.md` (KIT-070) |
| subagent profile | add `plugins/<plugin>/agents/<name>.md` in the plugin whose skills consume it (reachable through the dependency graph) with frontmatter validated by `platforms/ci/schemas/agent.schema.json`; Devin CLI/Desktop and Claude Code load the profiles, Devin Cloud uses managed Devins and Codex none (README § Platform behavior) |
| template | only for a long artifact a skill links (a spec, a project `AGENTS.md`); a short field list goes inline in the skill. Add `plugins/<plugin>/templates/<prefix>-<name>.md` (prefix `spec`, `doc` or `project`), link it from the skill, then run `python3 platforms/tools/gen_index.py` |
| plugin | create `plugins/<name>/` with `.devin-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `plugin.json`, then run `python3 platforms/tools/gen_index.py` for its `INDEX.md`; declare `requiredPlugins`/`dependencies` on the plugins it consumes; register it in the root meta-plugin `requiredPlugins`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`. Prefer a skill in `guardrails`: a second plugin is justified only by an audience that must not load `guardrails` (KIT-038, KIT-047). Renaming or removing a plugin adds the old name to the Claude marketplace `renames` map |

A rule uses this frontmatter shape:

```yaml
---
description: <what loads and when, at most 160 characters>
trigger: glob
globs:
  - "<glob>"
  - "<glob>"
---
```

`globs` must be a YAML sequence: Devin rejects a comma-separated string (`YAML parse error: globs: invalid type: string ..., expected a sequence`).

A folder gets a `README.md` only when its files need explanation; shape it with [`docs/templates/kit-readme.md`](../docs/templates/kit-readme.md). Outside the generated plugin indexes this repository has no `INDEX.md` (KIT-042). The `kit-*` templates shape kit content, so they live in `docs/templates/`, outside every plugin.

A subagent skill sets Devin `subagent: true` or a shared `agent: <plugin>:<profile>` (a bare name runs as `general-purpose`, KIT-114), plus Claude `context: fork` and `background: false`; named profiles must exist under `plugins/<plugin>/agents/` of a plugin reachable through the dependency graph.

Hooks are a guard, not a guardrail: they fail open, load in Claude Code, local Devin and, once the user trusts them, Codex (KIT-081), and cannot replace user confirmation or the always-on safety boundaries. Each hook's event, behaviour and tests: [`plugins/guardrails/hooks/README.md`](../plugins/guardrails/hooks/README.md).

## CI requirements

- Every pull request to `main` and every push to `main` runs `ci.yml`, `gitleaks.yml` and `codeql.yml`, which keep `workflow_dispatch` (KIT-076, superseding KIT-014's dispatch-only rule). Their jobs are the required checks `ci`, `workflow-lint`, `gitleaks`, `codeql (python)` and `codeql (actions)`; the sixth, `CodeQL`, is the code scanning result GitHub posts for the uploaded analysis and fails on a new alert in the changed code. A merge needs those six green and an independent review READY on the same head: the coordinator arms auto-merge only after the READY, and green checks alone never merge. A job's `name` is its check context, so a renamed job leaves the ruleset waiting; `platforms/ci/validations/test_kit_workflows.py` pins the names (each workflow's whole list of contexts, the required ones once each), the triggers (`pull_request`, never `pull_request_target`), the read-only default `permissions`, the per-ref `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress`, the actions pinned by commit SHA and the gitleaks scan range. No job carries an `if`, except `ci`, which gathers the pull request layers (KIT-077): it runs `if: always()` and passes only when each job it needs passed, since a skipped required job reports success.
- Every job, in `.github/workflows/` and in the templates of `platforms/kits/github/workflows/` (all `*.yml`), pins its actions by commit SHA with the version in a comment, pins each tool a run step downloads (just, gitleaks, actionlint, zizmor, Claude Code) by version and sha-256 instead of piping a script into a shell, grants a write scope only where `test_kit_workflows.py` lists the job (`write-all` counts as every scope), sets `persist-credentials` on its checkout (`false`, or `true` with the reason in the file, as `ci-godot.yml`'s `git lfs pull` needs), passes `${{ }}` values to `run:` through `env:` and sets `timeout-minutes` to 3 × the longest measured green run of that job, rounded up to 5 minutes, at least 5; GitHub's 360-minute limit for a hosted job is the ceiling, and a job with no green run yet (`evals.yml`) carries that limit until its first green run (KIT-076 lists the runs). `test_kit_workflows.py` checks all of these in both folders.
- `ci.yml`'s `workflow-lint` job runs actionlint and zizmor, pinned by version and sha-256, over `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `platforms/kits/github/workflows/*.yml`, and zizmor over the composite actions projects pin (`platforms/ci/actions/*/action.yml`, KIT-081; actionlint reads workflows only); any finding fails it. zizmor runs at its default persona with online audits; a finding is fixed, and silenced in a config or comment only as a documented false positive with its reason. Locally: `zizmor .github/workflows/*.yml platforms/kits/github/workflows/*.yml platforms/ci/actions/*/action.yml`. The pedantic persona still lists jobs without a `name`, workflows without job-level `concurrency` and `ci-godot.yml`'s container tag, which follows the `godot-version` input.
- Each test layer has one place and one trigger (KIT-077). Every `platforms/ci/validations/test_*.py` module sets `LAYER` (`unit`: in-process, no subprocess or git; `contract`: the kit's own files read in-process; `integration`: scripts, git, throwaway repositories; `functional`: the kit synced into `platforms/ci/fixtures/consumer/`, then that project's own checks, and the whole `smoke.sh`; `performance`: the hooks' latency budgets). A class, or one test method (`test_x.LAYER = "performance"` after it), may set its own, and an integration class lists in `COVERS` the globs of the files it exercises. `platforms/tools/run_tests.py` (also `platforms/tools/check.sh --tests`) selects by layer and runs the tests in parallel worker processes; a test class without a layer, or an integration class without `COVERS`, is a usage error, and `test_run_tests.py` checks that every `COVERS` glob names a kit file.
- Locally, an implementer runs only the TDD loop and the linters: `platforms/tools/check.sh --tests --layer unit,contract` (about 1 s), plus `platforms/tools/check.sh --tests <the test modules covering the changed files>`; CI runs the rest on the pushed head (timings: the KIT-077 record). A reviewer reads that result and runs nothing else, except a gate or proof with no result recorded for the head (once, on a clean checkout) and a targeted probe at a security boundary (skill `review` § 2). The linters: `check.sh` (`check_kit.py`, whose § 13 parses the scripts with bash 3.2 on macOS, which the Ubuntu runner cannot; `check_changelog.py`, which fails a CHANGELOG line added under a released version, as a rebase across a release can leave (KIT-109); `gen_index.py --check`; `claude plugin validate` when Claude Code is installed), `shellcheck` on a changed script, actionlint and zizmor on a changed workflow. Run `smoke.sh` too when the change touches a script it runs: on macOS it runs them under bash 3.2. Always `gitleaks git --redact --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD"` before the push, because a secret pushed to this public repository is exposed before any check runs.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the pull request layers as parallel jobs (KIT-077): `static` (ShellCheck at its default severity with `-x` on tools/kits, the Claude Code install, `check.sh --links`), `unit` (gdtoolkit from `platforms/kits/godot/requirements-gdtoolkit.txt`, then `run_tests.py --layer unit,contract`), `integration (1)` to `integration (3)` (that gdtoolkit and the pinned `just` and `gitleaks`, then `run_tests.py --layer integration --changed-from HEAD^1 --shard N/3`: only the integration classes whose `COVERS` or own module the change touches, every class when it touches code under `platforms/`, `plugins/` or the root manifest folders, or `VERSION`, that no `COVERS` names, and every class on a dispatch), and `red` (`platforms/tools/ci_red.py`: `review_checks.py red` on the merge commit, the verdict in the job summary; NONE passes only when the PR body's `## Red` opens with `Exception`; the body is read when the job runs, so a re-run sees an edited body, #294). The required `ci` job needs `static`, `unit`, the integration shards and `red` (#281: the red check is required on every pull request), so only a red FAIL fails it. Durations: the KIT-077 record.
- `.github/workflows/ci-full.yml`: the whole integration layer in three shards and the functional layer (the fixture consumer project and the whole `smoke.sh`), on every push to `main`, nightly and on demand. `.github/workflows/performance.yml`: the latency budgets alone on a runner, nightly and on demand, one test at a time. Neither is a required check.
- Scripts under `platforms/` must parse under bash 3.2 (macOS `/bin/bash`, the `smoke.sh` restricted PATH): avoid unquoted text after a quoted string inside `"$(...)"` — write `"$(basename "$f")"`/`"${f##*/}"` instead of `"$(basename "$f" .md)"` — and an odd number of apostrophes in a heredoc inside `"$(...)"`, a comment's `it's` included. `check_kit.py` § 13 runs `bash -n` on every `*.sh` with the bash on `PATH`, so on macOS it catches what `shellcheck` and the Ubuntu bash 5 accept (KIT-060).
- `check_kit.py` also gates allowed tools, three-way user-only/subagent/rule parity, reference kinds/sources, hooks, backtick paths, links that leave their plugin and a skill description's literal `Use when` and `Not for` (KIT-052), and shell syntax with `bash -n` (KIT-060).
- `check.sh` also runs `gen_index.py --check`: every `plugins/*/INDEX.md` is generated from the plugin's files, so a stale one fails and the message prints `python3 platforms/tools/gen_index.py`. Never edit a plugin `INDEX.md` by hand (KIT-040).
- `.github/workflows/gitleaks.yml`: the gitleaks CLI pinned by version and sha-256, with `--redact` and no token; a pull request scans its own commits (base..head), a push to `main` and a dispatch the whole history.
- `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`: CodeQL advanced setup for `python` and `actions` with `build-mode: none` (KIT-063), also weekly (`schedule`), so new queries reach a quiet `main`. GitHub disables a public repository's scheduled workflows after 60 days without activity; re-enable it in the Actions tab. Default setup stays off, because GitHub rejects the advanced-setup SARIF upload while it is on. The repository's secret scanning and push protection complement gitleaks, which stays the local pre-push check.
- `.github/workflows/evals.yml`: on-demand `claude plugin eval plugins` over the cases of every plugin; needs the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` repository secret, which is not set (owner 2026-10-06), so nothing runs it on a schedule.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: first `platforms/tools/release_guard.py` (KIT-077): the tagged commit needs a green `ci-full` run. The guard waits up to 20 min while that run is not created, queued or in progress, and fails on a completed run that is not green or on the timeout, so no release is published. It never deletes or moves the tag (the ruleset `protect-release-tags` forbids deleting a `v*` tag): re-run `release.yml` once `ci-full` is green on that commit (`gh run rerun <id>`), or release the next patch version. Then the tag/version validation and the release creation.
- `.github/dependabot.yml` updates the `github-actions` pins weekly in `/` (`.github/workflows/`), in `/platforms/kits/github/workflows`, in `/platforms/ci/actions/spec-tools` and in `/platforms/ci/actions/gitleaks` (KIT-084), so the templates projects copy and the actions they pin stay current too.

## Evals

- Cases live in `plugins/<plugin>/evals/<case>/` (`prompt.md` plus `graders/*.md`, `case.yaml` and `fixture.sh` when the case needs a repository); a case without a grader fails to load, and `check_kit.py` rejects a case folder without `prompt.md` or `case.yaml`, or without `graders/*.md`.
- The suite holds sixteen cases: the six `trigger` cases below; two `negative` cases for `sdd-intake`, which check what the skill must not do (#401: a finding stays out of its §§ 1–3, and a repository with no `docs/spec/` does not load it; their graders use `tool_used` with `min: 0` and `max: 0`, and the first an `llm` grader too, and each repeats the `sdd-intake` trigger bullet in `append_system_prompt` like a `trigger` case); one behavior case, tagged `ready`, for each of three critical skills: `session`, `review` and `git`; and five cases tagged `rule`, one per behavior KIT-070 moved from a skill into a path rule (`code`, `godot`, `java`, `protocol`, `tests`; #275). A `rule` case's `fixture.sh` writes the `CLAUDE.md` marker `sync-project.sh` writes, with a profile that selects its rule, and copies no rule, and the prompt reads a file the rule's globs match, so the plugin's path-rule hook gives the rule as it does in a synced project (KIT-081 stage 3); the scaffold stops when it cannot reach the hook or the rule. Before stage 3 the fixture copied the rule into `.claude/rules/`: by hand on 2026-11-16 (Claude Code 2.1.287, 5 runs per case), the hook scored as the copy did (the KIT-081 record has the method and numbers). They were written in KIT-080 and not run (the Docker store below); `ready` follows their first scores. The coverage and mutation commands of the removed `testing-gdscript-*` cases need no case: they are optional, advisory tools in the user-only `sdd-implement` reference `test-gates.md`, which a model-run eval does not load. A case never names its skill; its `skill-fired` grader checks that the skill fired. Another grader is `tool_used` or `regex` when the output can be matched; an `llm` grader states one PASS and one FAIL line, and a plausible wrong answer meets the FAIL line.
- Before opening a pull request that changes a skill, a rule or an agent (`plugins/*/skills/**`, `plugins/*/rules/**`, `plugins/*/agents/**`, `plugins/guardrails/AGENTS.md`), the implementer runs the evals by hand and the PR body cites the command and the score on an `Evals:` line; the review checks that the line is there. The run is at least the cases below that the change touches, or the `trigger` suite when none does. `evals.yml` stays dispatch-only, with no Anthropic secret in Actions: GitHub cannot host a Claude Code run with the plugin.
- A change to the `description` of one of those three skills reruns its case by hand before the PR. A new skill, or a change to another skill, needs no new case (KIT-037).
- Six cases tagged `trigger` measure whether a plain request loads a cross-cutting skill: `git`, `session`, `investigate`, `security`, `review` and `sdd-intake` (#245; the `parallelize` case went with KIT-070: 0.00 over 5 runs, while Claude ran the checks in parallel without the skill), each with only its `skill-fired` grader (KIT-071). A run loads no `CLAUDE.md`, so each case repeats its skill's trigger bullet from `plugins/guardrails/AGENTS.md`, without the `- `, in `append_system_prompt`, and `check_kit.py` fails when the two differ or a `trigger` case has none. A change to a trigger bullet or to one of those six descriptions reruns its case: `claude plugin eval plugins --tag trigger --runs 5 --ablation none --no-publish --trust-plugin --scaffold --output-dir "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/kit-evals"`, plus `--allow-tools Bash` where the Docker store below allows it. The target is a score of at least 0.8 per case.
- Locally: `claude plugin eval plugins --case '<name>' --runs 1 --ablation none --no-publish --trust-plugin --output-dir "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/kit-evals"` (add `--scaffold --allow-tools Bash Edit Write` for cases with a fixture). The target is `plugins`, because a `plugins:` entry loads only from inside the target directory; a case `plugins:` entry outside it fails the case load with "outside the containment root" (KIT-041). `--output-dir` keeps the aggregate result out of `plugins/evals/results/`, which `check_kit.py` would read as a plugin without a manifest. The evals workflow runs only cases tagged `ready`, with a pinned model and judge.
- Before a local run, `claude auth status` must exit 0 (`"loggedIn": true`). Logged out, every case stops before any model turn: the command exits 2 in about a second and the result reads `casesPassed: 0` and `overallScore: 0`, like a skill that fails every grader; only `partialReason: "auth_failed"` and the arm's `error` ("Not logged in · Please run /login") say that nothing ran. A `--scaffold` case also stops, with exit 1, when `~/.docker` holds a symbolic link (Docker Desktop's `~/.docker/bin`), which the Bash sandbox cannot exclude. Record such a case as unverified with that line, never as a failing skill, and rerun it after `claude auth login`.

## After merging to main

- Devin Cloud needs no manual refresh; it fetches `main` for each session.
- Devin CLI/Desktop re-fetches at app start; run `devin plugins update` to force it.
- Codex and Claude Code refresh through launchd and `platforms/tools/refresh.sh`; run `platforms/tools/doctor.sh` to diagnose local state.
- In Claude Code, use `/doctor prompt-audit` to inspect loaded instructions and `/context` to inspect token cost.
